query:
A 14-year-old child presents with left-sided chest pain and a fever. A chest X-ray (Figure 1) shows evidence of pleural effusion. Given the clinical history of sudden onset chest pain radiating to the shoulder and fever, what is the most likely cause of the pleural effusion observed on the chest X-ray, considering only the X-ray findings?
A) Left-sided pneumonia leading to parapneumonic effusion
B) Haemothorax caused by spontaneous rib spur rupture
C) Viral pleuritis resulting in pleural effusion
D) Congestive heart failure causing bilateral pleural effusion
E) Tuberculous pleuritis causing pleural effusion
F) Trauma-induced haemothorax
